name: hosted-cloud-tier-foundation
title: Hosted-Cloud-Tier (Tier 3) Foundation
description:
Research and lay groundwork for offering Vrooli itself as a hosted-cloud subscription tier (Tier 3 per docs/monetization/PRICING.md). The current Tier 1 self-host pitch in docs/monetization/catalog/base/business.md positions web-console as a tool for operators who already manage their own infrastructure — a real audience but a small one. Tier 3 expands the addressable market by giving subscribers a managed Vrooli instance they can connect to from any device (notably phone), unlocking the use cases web-console and GCT cannot serve in self-host-only form.

This is intentionally distinct from initiative remote-deployment-ops, which addresses a different concern: making Vrooli internal deployment workflow operable from non-shell surfaces (operator ergonomics for shipping Vrooli releases). The names are similar; the concerns are not. remote-deployment-ops items stay where they are.

Filed as one of three infrastructure initiatives surfaced on the 2026-04-25 vision walk (others: design-language-foundation [priority 7, top of three], browser-automation-studio-readiness [TBD]). Operator framed the 2026-04-25 walk repositioning as option C: the catalog headliner status of web-console stays accurate for self-hosters; Tier 3 launches as an additional offering. No depends_on edge is added to web-console-readiness — both pitches coexist by design. The portfolio decision filed alongside this initiative captures that framing.

Known gaps to workshop (not items yet):
- VPS provider research: DigitalOcean / Hetzner / Linode / Fly.io comparative analysis (price, region coverage, operational maturity, billing API, snapshot semantics)
- Cloudflare tunnel UX research: subdomain provisioning model (vrooli.app/<customer> subdomain vs customer-owned domain bring-your-own), DNS automation, certificate handling
- Auth/identity research: does customer instance inherit identity from LPBS user-auth-service, or run a separate per-instance auth? Single-sign-on between LPBS account and hosted Vrooli instance is the seam
- Billing add-on integration: how does the Tier 3 upgrade flow plug into existing LPBS Stripe integration? Per-instance metering vs flat subscription
- Minimum-viable Vrooli surface for the hosted offering: which scenarios must run for the offering to deliver value (web-console core? full business-bundle? everything?)
- Onboarding flow: from Stripe checkout → instance provisioned → operator credentials issued → first connection. End-to-end UX must be specified before build.
- Customer offboarding: data export when subscription ends, instance teardown, customer-owned-data retention policy
- SLA / support model: pre-launch can be light, but the framework must exist before pricing can be set
- Operational tooling: how does Vrooli (the company) monitor and operate N customer instances? Same question every SaaS faces; needs explicit answer
- Pricing: depends on monetization pricing-trough decision (currently deferred to 2026-05-09 pending Stripe→PRICING.md sync)

Not in scope (cross-edges, not items here):
- Existing web-console-readiness work — stays separate. This initiative provides the deployment surface; web-console-readiness provides the product running on it.
- GCT cluster — same shape. Customer hosted instances can run GCT once GCT ships.
- Subscription / billing surface in LPBS — already exists; Tier 3 plugs into it but does not own it.
- remote-deployment-ops — different concern, stays separate.

See orchestration-summary.md for sequencing, decisions, and pattern notes.
